title: Kyoto in five days
summary: Twelve notes become one walkable plan, from the northern temples to the morning market, with fares, meals and rainy-day alternatives kept together. All places and prices are fictional.

sections.heading: The five-day shape
sections.content: Keep one base for five days. Visit northern temples, east-bank lanes, West Valley bamboo, South Town market and crafts, then the morning market before departure. Book one timed activity daily and leave 90 minutes after lunch. Riverbank House, 8 Bluestone Road, Kawamachi, is ¥9,800 a double per night without breakfast, six minutes from the metro. Check in at 3pm and out at 10am, with bag storage available. Four nights cost ¥39,200, shared between two. Pine Lantern Hostel is ¥8,600 nightly with smaller rooms and easier airport transfers. Allow 15 extra minutes to the station from the riverside. It is quiet after 9pm, so keep rolling bags quiet on the stone lanes.

sections.heading: Temples and walks, grouped by place
sections.content: Start the northern day at Paper Lantern Temple at 7am, 12 Cedar Lane, Kitayama, ¥600. Walk 12 minutes from the station via the eastern steps. It is quiet before 8:15. Continue 18 minutes to Maple Well Hall, open 9am, ¥400, then Little Stream Temple, ¥300 cash. The east bank runs 3.2km from Bluestone Bridge to Willow Exit in about 80 minutes with four rest points. The main path is gentle. The old-lane detour has steps in its first 1.1km. Respect yellow-rope closures and allow 12 minutes onward to the metro. Reach West Valley’s north exit before 9am on day three. Walk the 1.8km bamboo path, then turn east downhill at Stone Bridge for a 3.6km station loop. The west gate adds 120 steps. Buy water at the station, rest on the two bridge benches and watch wet ground.

sections.heading: Transport and the budget
sections.content: At the fictional fares, buses cost ¥230, metro rides ¥260 and a day pass ¥1,100. Around five included rides make a pass worthwhile. Three northern buses cost ¥690, two east-bank metro rides ¥520 and four South Town buses ¥920, so skip the pass on those days. The ¥720 West Valley return train is excluded. Walk on day five. Prepare change before boarding and check maps at stops. Allow ¥2,850 per person for transport, including the ¥720 airport shuttle but excluding intercity travel. Food is ¥3,200 daily, ¥16,000 across five days. Three temples cost ¥1,300 and the museum ¥700. Half the room bill is ¥19,600. With ¥3,000 contingency, budget about ¥43,450 per person before shopping or the optional ¥2,800 class.

sections.heading: Food, addresses and hours
sections.content: Blue Tile Kitchen, 6 Lantern Lane, Kawamachi, serves a ¥1,450 tofu set, 5–9pm, last orders 8:15pm, closed Wednesday. Mushroom rice contains fish stock, so ask about dietary needs. Wellside Noodles, 14 Well Road, opens 11:30am–7:30pm with ¥980 soba and ¥250 kelp soup. Slow Flame, 3 East Bridge, has ten seats and ¥2,100 dinner. Book the day before. East Bridge Snack Hut in West Valley opens 10am, taking cash for ¥220 rice balls and ¥180 miso soup. Moss Garden Teahouse opens 10:30am–4:30pm, closed Thursday, with ¥520 roasted tea and ¥380 rice cake. Rainy-day Paper Window Coffee opens 11am–6pm, closed Monday. A latte is ¥580 and pumpkin toast ¥680.

sections.heading: Rain and market alternatives
sections.content: In heavy rain, swap the east bank for the Woodcraft Museum, ¥700, 10am–5pm, closed Tuesday. Allow 70 minutes, store large umbrellas and keep cameras out of galleries. Walk eight minutes to Paper Window Coffee, then use covered South Town Market and return from its station. Stalls open from 9:30am and mostly close at 4pm. Half open on Sunday. Green Leaf Tea sells 40g roasted tea for ¥900 with one tasting. Bean House hot soy milk is ¥300, ¥20 off with your own cup. Wooden Spoon Studio’s carved spoons cost ¥1,600 and its 2pm sanding class ¥2,800, booked two days ahead. Buy cups on the second circuit and recycle cardboard at the exit.

sections.heading: What to carry
sections.content: Use a 20-litre daypack and small case. Wear grippy shoes, keep an umbrella in the side pocket and carry ¥5,000 cash. Save the lodging address, return service and a map for each day offline. Separate the power bank from water. Back up photos and video nightly. Wrap cups in clothes and protect the camera. Ask the hostel for newspaper to dry shoes. Plan rest points, check maps in wider spaces and move your backpack to the front in crowds. If you start late, drop a stop instead of rushing the whole day.

sources.title: Pack light for five walking days

sections.heading: The last morning and departure
sections.content: Kawamachi Morning Market opens Saturdays, 7:30–10:30am. Valley Bakery’s ¥280 red-bean rolls often sell out before 9am, but protect the return journey. Collect stored bags before 10am check-out. Walk 15 minutes from Kawamachi exit to the airport shuttle stop, pay ¥720 and arrive 25 minutes early. If the market is closed, station-side Pine Lantern Breakfast opens at 6:30am with a ¥650 porridge set. All venues, locations and fares are fictional demo information.
